text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing correlated GPU signals on gw-rtx-04 over the last 10m: ECC correctable spikes, short thermal blips, and two Xid 13 resets. One inference pod OOM/killed mid-run. Thinking we should try a soft-quarantine flow rather than insta-drain.

raj: saw a similar transient on gw-rtx-07 ~8m ago. Our current rule (Xid > 5 within 30s -> cordon+drain) is triggering on bus resets. We should avoid requeueing long training/inference jobs for flakiness.

sophie: +1. Proposal for k8s path: soft-quarantine stage that prevents new pods, runs a fast verification, then decides. Flow sketch:
- taint node: `gpu-quarantine=true:NoSchedule` and cordon so no new pods land
- launch `memtest-light` job + NVML checker (5-10m)
- if pass -> remove taint + uncordon
- if fail -> cordon+drain + mark for replacement

infra-bot: alert created: GPU_HEALTH_MULTI_SIGNAL node=gw-rtx-04 severity=warning metrics=[nvidia.ecc.correctable_rate,nvidia.xid.count,hw.temp.gpu] ts=1870012345

nora: ops/cost note — false positives are painful for Dedicated pools. Suggest pool-aware hysteresis: production/dedicated pools get longer verification windows and higher Xid thresholds; burst/test pools use lower hysteresis.

raj: Slurm path differs: fencing a slurm node forces immediate requeues. For Slurm-dedicated nodes we should set a maintenance flag and notify the scheduler to drain gracefully or wait for checkpoints. Dual-path logic: k8s->soft-quarantine; slurm->maintenance + notify.

leo: draft controller config (feature gated):
```
controller: node-autocheck
feature_flag: soft_quarantine_v1
soft_quarantine:
  enabled: true
  taint: gpu-quarantine=true:NoSchedule
  verify_job: memtest-light
  verify_timeout_seconds: 600
  xid_threshold: 4
  ecc_rate_threshold: 0.025
  hysteresis_window_seconds: 300
  force_drain_after_seconds: 3600
```
If verify_job exits non-zero -> escalate to full drain + annotate node with failure reason and S3 telemetry link.

sophie: telemetry: capture last 300s of `nvidia.*` and `node_exporter` snapshots and attach as S3 link in node annotation so postmortems have metrics. Also increment `node_soft_quarantine_count`.

maya: add blacklist cooldown: if node fails verification twice in 24h mark for 12h quarantine/blacklist to avoid flapping. Also annotate with `recovery_attempts` counter.

nora: runbook items: vendor memtest step, RMA url, and a simple cost estimator to compare RMA vs replace/keep. Ops should get an automated ticket when node escalates.

raj: rollout plan: 1) implement controller behind feature flag 2) unit + e2e tests 3) canary on `eng-gpu-pool` (non-prod) for 48h 4) staged rollout to Dedicated pools with higher thresholds -> then to prod.

leo: I'll open PR with controller skeleton, CRD schema, and a metric `node_soft_quarantine_count`. Can we also export `node_quarantine_duration_seconds` for SLO tracking?

sophie: verification job details: memtest-light runs for up to 10m, checks ECC counters pre/post delta, validates GPU temperature and bus reset rates. Return codes: 0=pass, 1=transient-fail (retry once), 2=hard-fail. Controller should treat 1 as a single retry before escalate.

maya: assignment: leo -> PR + metrics; sophie -> verification job + telemetry S3 payload; raj -> slurm maintenance path + scheduler integration; nora -> runbook + cost estimator. I'll shepherd the canary and monitor alerts.

sophie: also add `force_drain_after_seconds` param for emergencies (default 3600) so nodes don't hold capacity forever if jobs don't finish.

maya: scheduling the canary for Monday 09:00 UTC, 48h watch window. If no objections we roll. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: noted participants: maya, raj, sophie, nora, leo. Canary window: start=1870015600 end=1870188400 monitoring=48h

maya: thanks all — we'll keep an eye on gw-rtx-04. If the verify job passes we uncordon and log everything. If it fails twice we'll mark for replacement and kick the RMA flow.
